title: Anand at nightfall
hookLine: the six ceremony pauris close the day in joy

lines: A LONG DAY. A PLATE PUT DOWN.
YOU DIDN'T ASK. IT'S JUST THERE.
cards: A long day. You walk in, drop your bag, and before you've even sat down, someone puts a plate in front of you. Hot dal, a roti folded on the side, maybe a little achaar.
You didn't ask. It's just there. Nobody makes a speech about it.
You just sit. Safe first, then fed. That's the order the evening prayer follows too.
Yesterday, the shelter. Today, the plate.

teach.h: AFTER SHELTER, THE SIX PAURIS OF JOY.
teach.b: After the Chaupai asks for shelter, Rehras turns to joy: the six pauris of the Anand, the first five and the fortieth. You know them now. Anand bhaiaa meree maae: joy has come, my mother.
And at the very end, anad sunahu vaddabhaageeho: hear the bliss, you fortunate ones. Notice the order inside Rehras. First, protect me.

teach.h: PROTECT ME, THEN JOY HAS COME.
teach.b: Then, joy has come. Fear is spoken to before joy is sung. And the joy isn't a reward for a good day.
It's just what the night is given. Then, after the Anand, Rehras closes with two short passages that also come at the very end of the Guru Granth Sahib.
The first is called the Mundavani, often explained as the seal, and it has a dinner-table picture of its own.

teach.h: MUNDAVANI: A PLATE OF TRUTH, CONTENTMENT.
teach.b: In paraphrase, by Guru Arjan: on this plate, three things have been placed: truth, contentment and contemplation. The nectar of the Name is set there too, the support of all. Whoever eats it, whoever enjoys it, is saved.
The second is a slok, also by Guru Arjan, a short, grateful confession.
In paraphrase: I didn't appreciate what You did for me; You made me worthy. I have no virtue; You took pity on me, and I met the True Guru, my friend. So the evening prayer ends at a table.
Shelter, then joy, then a plate with truth, contentment and reflection on it, and a thank you for what you didn't earn.

how: In Rehras Sahib, the Benti Chaupai and its savaiya and dohra are followed by six pauris of the Anand, then the Mundavani and a slok by Guru Arjan, the passages that also close the Guru Granth Sahib.

o: bliss, a deep and settled joy
a feast served at the close of prayers
a loud cheer when a ceremony ends

games.q: the end of Rehras — tap the pairs.
p: the first five and the fortieth

s: in Rehras the Anand comes before the Chaupai
the Chaupai's plea for shelter comes first; then the six pauris of joy.
the Mundavani comes at the very end of the Guru Granth Sahib
it and the slok after it, both by Guru Arjan, close the scripture before the Raagmala.
the Mundavani's plate holds truth, contentment and contemplation
and the nectar of the Name, the support of all.

games.q: Rehras has just asked for shelter as night comes. what does it do next?
o: sings joy: the six pauris of the Anand.
games.why: after protect me comes joy has come, and then the Mundavani's plate of truth, contentment and contemplation.

practice: Sit back as if you've just come home and the plate is in front of you, and hum or softly say, two or three times: anand bhaiaa meree maae, satguroo mai paaiaa, joy has come, my mother, I have found the True Guru.
Then picture the plate, truth, contentment, a moment of reflection, and take one thing from it for tonight.

wordCard.voice: Anand, joy: in Rehras, after the Chaupai's plea for shelter, the six pauris of the Anand bring joy, and the Mundavani sets a plate of truth, contentment and contemplation.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: thaal, a plate; the Mundavani says three things are placed on it: truth, contentment and contemplation.

carryVoice: Your line: joy at dusk. Safe first, then fed, and a thank you for what wasn't earned. Until tomorrow.

sources.ref: Ramkali M3, Anand, pauris 1–5 and 40, Ang 917–922
Mundavani M5 and Slok M5, Ang 1429
Sikh Rehat Maryada, on the contents of Rehras
